note: Derived reading aid. Never authoritative; never read as intent (Decision 0004). The Plan document governs.
author: Lightweight model draft for Clara (technical writing) via Claudia Atlas <claudia.atlas@agents.arcadia.local>
title: Cap every production session's token spend
purpose: Each production session should be limited by a platform token ceiling and by a probe that checks it can do its work. A session that cannot write should not waste the budget, and every stop should clear from the to-do page in two clicks at most.
serves: The Project outcome of unattended production staying within its spend, with the operator asked only when needed.
done_when: A session that reaches its ceiling or cannot write the workspace stops with one named blocker, and that blocker clears from the to-do page in two clicks at most.
reading_note: Draft: 6 of the 9 Actions are done. Open items are the one-click clear for every blocker kind, the probe result on the reconcile receipt, and keeping the pointer in step with queue reorders.

actions.title: Replay a recorded no-write session as a test
actions.why: A recorded failure replayed as a test catches the same waste without spending tokens again.
actions.done_when: A fast replay of a recorded session that could not write ends stopped before its token bound, with exactly one named blocker and no second launch.

actions.title: Record one validated row per session
actions.why: Replaces estimated prose with exact per-session cost and defect data for the next decision.
actions.done_when: Each session has one row with its cost, review findings, touches and outcome, and a malformed row fails the check.

actions.title: Stop a session when it reaches its token ceiling
actions.why: Platform limits, not prompt discipline, must bound spend, because a heavy task once ran unmetered.
actions.done_when: A session that reaches its ceiling stops with a budget record showing cached and uncached tokens, is not relaunched, and the ceiling cannot be raised from a prompt or brief.

actions.title: Probe the session's own sandbox before real work
actions.why: Only a probe run inside the session shows whether it can actually write and validate.
actions.done_when: A failing probe ends the attempt with one named environment blocker, and a passing probe records its token use within budget.

actions.title: Clear each blocker kind from the to-do page in two clicks
actions.why: Each new blocker kind arrived without a remote clear, so the operator had to use the command line.
actions.done_when: A check fails when a blocker kind has no registered clear, and each registered clear is a button that resolves in at most two interactions.

actions.title: Position new actions during activation without disturbing the queue
actions.why: Activation left Actions unpositioned and the pointer stale, which needed manual repair.
actions.done_when: Activating a plan leaves other Projects' queue order unchanged, and the sync step retries a temporary database lock.

actions.title: Record revised roles and a compact session brief
actions.why: Lead sessions had grown large, so each session should start from a short generated brief.
actions.done_when: The guidance records the revised roles and a brief template, and every role leaves one ledger row.

actions.title: Attach the probe result to the reconcile receipt
actions.why: The receipt should carry the probe evidence, so a stop can be checked afterwards.
actions.done_when: A refused session's receipt includes the probe result and its budget, verified against a real provider sandbox.

actions.title: Keep the pointer in step with queue reorders
actions.why: A moved queue item should not leave the current pointer on the wrong Action.
actions.done_when: A reordered queue and its pointer change settle together, and a test reproduces the post-activation lock and shows the queue is valid afterwards.
